title: Using Your Head
coreMove: Slow the mind down enough to test easy stories, analogies, and preferred interpretations.
sourcePressure: The close shifts to disciplined thinking habits: skepticism, analogy risk, active judgment, and resistance to wishful interpretation under pressure. Frozen source has no chapter-specific named figure, study, place, or event beyond the visible title/support notes; use conceptual source terms only and do not invent anchors.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using your head means being smarter, more rational, or more confident.

skillTargets: distinguish disciplined thinking from its generic imitation in a new scenario

tryThisNowSpec: In 30 to 90 seconds, write the current decision as one obstacle, one chosen response, and one action that would visibly test disciplined thinking in your actual situation.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
